# **<mark>ICSG PRESS RELEASE                                             Date Issued: 21</mark>**<sup>**st**</sup> **<mark>August 2012</mark>** 



## **Copper: Preliminary Data for May 2012** 

The International Copper Study Group (ICSG) released preliminary data for May 2012 world copper supply and demand in its August 2012 Copper Bulletin. The Bulletin is available for sale upon request. 

According to preliminary ICSG data, the refined copper market balance for May 2012 showed a production deficit of 21,000 metric tonnes (t). When making seasonal adjustments for world refined production and usage, May showed a production surplus of 42,000 t. The apparent refined copper balance for the first five months of 2012, including revisions to data previously presented, indicates a production deficit of 405,000 t (a seasonally adjusted deficit of 291,000 t). This compares with a production deficit of 98,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of 21,000 t) in the same period of 2011. 

During the first five months of 2012, world apparent usage grew by 8.3% compared with that in the same period of 2011: A growth of 30% in China’s apparent usage* more than offset an aggregated decline of 6.2% in usage in Japan, the European Union and the United States.  China’s apparent usage growth was based on a 94% increase in net imports of refined copper.  However, comparative net imports in the first five months of 2011 were weak and anecdotal evidence suggests that the high import level in the first months of 2012 was accompanied by increased inventories held in bonded warehouses.  On a regional basis, usage grew by 18% in Asia, remained practically unchanged in the Americas, and declined by 8% in Europe, 14% in Oceania, and 8.5% in Africa. 

In the first five months of 2012, world mine production increased by 2.4% compared with production in the same period of 2011. Concentrate production increased by 0.6% while solvent extraction-electrowinning (SX-EW) was up by 9.5%.  Increases in Chile (1.5%), China (28%), Democratic Republic of the Congo (22%), Mexico (29%) and the United States (4.6%) more than offset declines in Indonesia (48%) and Zambia (6.8%).  On a regional basis, production rose by 3.6% in Africa, 1.5% in Asia, 3.9% in Europe and 3% in the Americas, but declined by 3% in Oceania.  The average world mine capacity utilization rate for the first five months of 2012 remained practically unchanged at around 77.8%. 

World refined production increased by 4.5% in the first five months of 2012 compared with refined production in the same period of 2011: primary production was up by 4% (mainly due to the increase in electrowon production) and secondary production (from scrap) increased by 6.9%.  The main contributors to growth were China (+12%), Japan (+13.7%) and the DRC (+31%) with production declining by 4.8% in Chile and 2.2% in the United States, the latter owing to a series of smelter maintenance shutdowns.  The average world refinery capacity utilization rat

e for the first five months of 2012 increased slightly to 79% from 78.5% in the same period of 2011. The average LME cash price for July 2012 was US$7,589.39 per tonne, up from the June average of US$7,420.11 per tonne. The 2012 high and low copper prices through the end of July were US$8,658 and US$7,251.5 per tonne, respectively, and the average was US$8,020.30 per tonne. As of the end of July, copper stocks held at the major metal exchanges (LME, COMEX, SHFE) totalled 448,797 t, a decline of 95,814 t from stocks held at the end of December 2011 and an increase of 4,670 t from stock levels at the end of June 2012. Compared with the June levels, stocks were down at Comex and the LME and up at SHFE.
